headlines.text: Turkish habit of stashing gold "under the pillow' hurts economy, government says. For years, Turks have stashed their gold at home against a raining day, mistrustful of banks. Now the government says that tradition hurts the economy

Turks often keep gold as a hedge against inflation. It may be hurting Turkey's future. Billions of dollars worth of gold is held in Turkish households outside the banking system. The government aims to convince citizens to put it into the mainstream financial system to help the economy.
State of U.S. democracy reaches new low, report finds. A new global democracy report finds the U.S. at its lowest level of democratic performance in the 50 years it has been measured.

SCOTUS rejects Trump's mail voting limits. And, the Kennedy Center financial crisis. The Supreme Court has rejected Trump's mail-in voting restrictions ahead of the midterm elections. And, the Kennedy Center says it is on the brink of bankruptcy and could close soon.

Trump says Ukraine and Russia agreed to stop attacks on energy sites. In the face of soaring diesel prices, President Trump claims Ukraine and Russia have agreed to halt strikes on each other's energy sites.

NATO jets shoot down a drone in Lithuanian airspace. The incident came less than a day after NATO leaders pledged that strikes close to the alliance's territory would drive the trans-Atlantic organization to increase support for Kyiv.

Anthropic co-founder says slowing AI is a 'collective action problem'. Anthropic co-founder Jack Clark discusses growing concerns about artificial intelligence, recent warning signs and what he says companies should do to reduce the risks.

Israel is 'dismantling Palestinian life' says Israeli human rights group. One of the country's leading human rights organizations says Israel is dismantling all aspects of Palestinian life at a breakneck rate. The group has extensively documented what it says are the mechanisms Israel has used to "ethnically cleanse" the West Bank of Palestinians.

The producer of Fleabag and Baby Reindeer's tip for finding a hit? Don't look for one. Theatre producer Francesca Moody has a remarkable record of spotting shows that go on to have wide success. At the Edinburgh Fringe festival, she told NPR about what she looks for in a performance.
US Fed raises interest rates as inflation weighs on economy. The 25bps hike is the first raise in three years and comes ahead of critical midterm elections in the US.
Geopolitical divides fueling Security Council inaction, Guterres warns. Guterres calls for urgent Security Council reform, says geopolitical divides hindering action on global crises.
UK trade unions back motion to boycott and sanction Israel. Motion demands taking action to oppose the 'catastrophic destruction of Gaza' and Israeli settler violence.
Belarus frees 25 political prisoners in return for US sanctions relief. The Trump administration said more releases would be secured soon amid improved US-Belarus relations.
Kosovo’s former president guilty of war crimes. Hashim Thaci, former President of Kosovo and KLA leader, has been found guilty of war crimes in the Hague.
Why has the response to Nepal’s floods been so muted?. Because wealthy nations do not want to take responsibility for their role in the current climate crisis.
South Africa slams planned US sanctions over alleged racial discrimination. Trump administration falling for misinformation from 'fringe groups' alleging discrimination against white Afrikaners.
‘Nowhere to go’: Gaza’s damaged buildings turn deadly. A war-damaged building collapses in Gaza City, killing at least 21 Palestinians and exposing fears of unsafe ruins.
Neturei Karta: Opposing Zionism. Inside Neturei Karta, the ultra-Orthodox Jewish group that rejects Zionism, supports Palestinians fighting occupation.
Can the US government punish a university for boycotting Israel?. The US House passed a bill that could cut universities off from federal student aid if they boycott Israel.
Poll shows Americans are increasingly alarmed by AI’s ecological footprint. New poll finds over half of Americans fear AI-driven data centers will hike electricity costs and strain water supplies.
Malaysia offers to invite Myanmar leader in Rohingya repatriation push. Malaysia has invited Myanmar’s military ruler for a visit to the country in a bid to expedite Rohingya repatriation.
Angry Dutch farmers blamed for railway sabotage: What happened?. Farmers in the Netherlands have taken action in the past, protesting against the government’s nitrogen policy.
Ebola fight in DRC ‘far from over,’ warns WHO chief. The DRC faces a growing Ebola threat as cases soar in North Kivu, despite progress in other regions, says Tedros
Sweden expels Iran embassy employee, citing security concerns. Stockholm says Iran-backed groups are plotting against 'Jewish and Israeli interests' in the country.

Some on-air claims about Dominion Voting Systems were false, Fox News acknowledges in statement after deal is announced
Dominion still has pending lawsuits against election deniers such as Rudy Giuliani and Sidney Powell

Here are the 20 specific Fox broadcasts and tweets Dominion says were defamatory. • Fox-Dominion trial delay 'is not unusual,' judge says • Fox News' defamation battle isn't stopping Trump's election lies

Judge in Fox News-Dominion defamation trial: 'The parties have resolved their case'. The judge just announced in court that a settlement has been reached in the historic defamation case between Fox News and Dominion Voting Systems.

'Difficult to say with a straight face': Tapper reacts to Fox News' statement on settlement. A settlement has been reached in Dominion Voting Systems' defamation case against Fox News, the judge for the case announced. The network will pay more than $787 million to Dominion, a lawyer for the company said.

Millions in the US could face massive consequences unless McCarthy can navigate out of a debt trap he set for Biden. • DeSantis goes to Washington, a place he once despised, looking for support to take on Trump • Opinion: For the GOP to win, it must ditch Trump • Chris Christie mulling 2024 White House bid • Analysis: The fire next time has begun burning in Tennessee

White homeowner accused of shooting a Black teen who rang his doorbell turns himself in to face criminal charges. • 'A major part of Ralph died': Aunt of teen shot after ringing wrong doorbell speaks • 20-year-old woman shot after friend turned into the wrong driveway in upstate New York, officials say

Newly released video shows scene of Jeremy Renner's snowplow accident. Newly released body camera footage shows firefighters and sheriff's deputies rushing to help actor Jeremy Renner after a near-fatal snowplow accident in January. The "Avengers" actor broke more than 30 bones and suffered other severe injuries. CNN's Chloe Melas has more.
Jake Gyllenhaal and Jamie Lee Curtis spent the Covid-19 lockdown together. It's sourdough bread and handstands for Jake Gyllenhaal and Jamie Lee Curtis.
Toddler crawls through White House fence, prompts Secret Service response. A tiny intruder infiltrated White House grounds Tuesday, prompting a swift response from the US Secret Service.

Jamie Foxx remains hospitalized nearly a week after 'medical complication'. Jamie Foxx remains hospitalized in Georgia nearly a week after his daughter revealed the actor experienced a "medical complication," a source with knowledge of the matter told CNN on Monday.

A 13-year-old dies after participating in a Benadryl TikTok 'challenge'. A 13-year-old in Ohio has died after "he took a bunch of Benadryl," trying a dangerous TikTok challenge that's circulating online, according to a CNN affiliate and a GoFundMe account from his family.
See pizza delivery guy take out suspect fleeing police. Pizza guy delivers more than a pie, taking out a fleeing suspect. CNN's Jeanne Moos shows him putting his best foot forward.
Netflix is winding down its DVD business after 25 years. Netflix is officially winding down the business that helped make it a household name.

FTC chair Lina Khan warns AI could 'turbocharge' fraud and scams. Artificial intelligence tools such as ChatGPT could lead to a "turbocharging" of consumer harms including fraud and scams, and the US government has substantial authority to crack down on AI-driven consumer harms under existing law, members of the Federal Trade Commission said Tuesday.

Texas Senate candidate Talarico said US was 'backsliding' on democracy in resurfaced clip. James Talarico said Americans should look to Western Europe for democratic inspiration in a resurfaced clip that drew a blunt response from Elon Musk.

7 Republicans rebel against Trump, vote with Dems to rein in Iran war powers. House Republicans joined Democrats to pass a war powers resolution reining in Trump's military engagement in Iran beyond the 60-day threshold.

3 dead, 1 hospitalized after news helicopter crashes in Los Angeles commercial area. Three people are dead and one person is hospitalized after a news helicopter crashed between two commercial buildings in the Chatsworth area of Los Angeles, authorities said.

Stephen A. Smith calls out NBA star Kawhi Leonard for letting Clippers take the fall for salary cap scandal. ESPN's Stephen A. Smith called Kawhi Leonard "a gangster" for escaping with a $700,000 fine while the LA Clippers face historic NBA penalties.

Sally Field remembers shopping at Walmart with Dolly Parton: ‘Can you imagine all of us?’. Sally Field recalled her Walmart shopping trips with Dolly Parton and the lasting bond they forged on the set of "Steel Magnolias" decades ago.

Fourth Florida resident dies after contracting flesh-eating bacteria linked to oysters. Florida reports fourth Vibrio vulnificus death in 2026 as health officials warn about raw oysters, contaminated water and severe infections.

Sophie Cunningham says she's talked with NBA Commissioner Adam Silver amid search for WNBA's next commissioner. Sophie Cunningham says she's spoken with Adam Silver multiple times about the WNBA commissioner search and wants a leader who puts players first.

Justin Herbert did not seem too pleased with the Chargers after disastrous loss to Arizona Cardinals. Justin Herbert's terse postgame answers and alarming sack totals raised new concerns after the Los Angeles Chargers' lopsided loss to Arizona.

Washington Democrat claims majority of recent DHS arrestees posed 'no threat to public safety'. The Washington Democrat claimed that, for the first time this summer, the majority of people arrested by DHS "pose absolutely no threat to public safety."

Injured climber crawls ‘through the night’ to safety after falling 500 feet down California mountain. Mount Shasta rescue crews finds San Jose man in a remote cabin after a glissading accident at Shasta-Trinity National Forest.

Real Madrid faces controversy after three star players refuse to wear pro-Ceuta solidarity shirts before match. Kylian Mbappé, Vinícius Júnior and Ibrahima Konaté refused to wear pro-Ceuta solidarity shirts before Real Madrid's match against Elche on Tuesday.

Ms Rachel says backlash over her Gaza posts 'doesn't faze' her as she calls out celebrity silence. Children's YouTuber Ms. Rachel told Rolling Stone that backlash over her Gaza posts no longer fazes her after being accused of pushing anti-Israel messaging.

Airport X-ray shows terrifying object taped in carry-on to skip checked baggage fee. A traveler at Dane County Regional Airport in Wisconsin taped a knife inside her carry-on bag to avoid paying a $100 baggage fee ahead of a camping trip, the TSA reported.

Republican upsets party-backed rival to challenge first openly trans member of Congress. Delaware Republicans picked a nominee from a three-way primary to challenge Sarah McBride, the first transgender member of Congress, this November.

Iran’s drone hunt escalates as Tehran targets US spy tech to expose battlefield secrets. Drone experts warn Iran is launching coordinated capture missions targeting U.S. unmanned surface vessels in the Strait of Hormuz for intel.

Fed expected to raise interest rates. And, board votes to close Kennedy Center. The Fed is expected to raise interest rates today for the first time in three years. And, the Kennedy Center board voted yesterday to close the historic center.

EU's Ursula von der Leyen says she wants Canada to become an associate member. European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen on Wednesday proposed making Canada the European Union's first associate member, a striking overture as U.S. President Donald Trump's tariffs drive Ottawa closer to Europe.

Senators question Trump's picks for top health positions, including surgeon general. On Wednesday, the Senate committee on health holds a confirmation hearing for three top health officials, including surgeon general. Dr. Nicole Saphier is President Trump's third attempt to nominate a surgeon general.

Kosovo's ex-President Thaci convicted of war crimes, sentenced to 25 years in prison. A European Union-backed court convicted former Kosovo President Hashim Thaci of war crimes committed during his country's war for independence from Serbia and sentenced him to 25 years in prison.

Saudi Arabia calls an attempted Mecca attack a 'red line' as Houthis deny they did it. Saudi Arabia accused Yemen's Iran-backed Houthi rebels overnight of trying to attack Islam's holiest city, prompting condemnation from countries in the region but no sign of military support.

As campaign season gears up, AI-generated ads are everywhere. Data suggests many candidates are embracing AI this year to boost their image and portray their opponents unfavorably. But whether it will turn out voters remains unclear.

A Kansas girl ran off to join the circus and changed the tattoo world. One of the country's first known female tattoo artists was born on a Kansas farm. Maud Stevens Wagner ran off to join the circus and later became a tattoo legend.

The 500 colleges where former students aren't repaying their loans, and why. Federal data shows many borrowers who aren't paying their loans went to private, for-profit colleges — schools that often market to low-income students and rely on federal financial aid for revenue.
21 million women live in U.S. counties with limited birth control access. Because of a data lag, the current reality of access may be even worse.

The Fed is expected to raise interest rates for the first time in 3 years. The Fed is widely expected to raise its benchmark interest rate to combat stubborn inflation. That could make it more expensive to borrow money to buy a car or carry a balance on a credit card.
